author: OpenAI Codex, historical-assessments agent
changeNote: First complete 240-question assessment under the current 15 Values bank and scoring. Documented positions, user-authorised sound inferences and supported conditional neutral answers are distinguished. An independent evidence audit amended interpretation and source errors before archiving; substantive findings are recorded in review.notes. No 12Axes questions or scores were imported.

metadata.name: Nelson Mandela
metadata.description: South African president assessed through his constitutional transition, reconciliation programme, mixed economy and international diplomacy.
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 1994–1999; earlier writings are contextual only. Historical analogies to contemporary technologies are explicitly inferred, not claims that the subject answered a modern questionnaire. Coalition constraints and contradictions are identified by axis.
metadata.role: South African anti-apartheid leader and president

image.creator: © copyright John Mathew Smith 2001 / Kingkongphoto & www.celebrity-photos.com

sources.title: Constitution of South Africa: original 1996 rights and allocation of powers (consolidated text; later amendments excluded)
African Charter report: reproductive autonomy under the 1996 Act
Prohibited Persons: treatment of refugees and asylum seekers, 1998
I am prepared to die: Rivonia statement, 20 April 1964
Small Arms and Light Weapons: Africa — The Gun-Free South Africa Campaign (p. 15)

axes.brief: Mandela governed through competitive universal elections and a binding constitutional order, leaving after one term. Democratic participation does not establish support for every form of direct democracy.
axes.counterEvidence: ANC discipline and limited consultation on GEAR qualify his participatory record, without making it a rejection of electoral accountability.

answers.rationale: His elected presidency and voluntary departure support competitive renewal.
Expert advice did not replace universal electoral legitimacy.
Universal adult franchise was central to the settlement.
He accepted a constitution binding the executive and legislature.
The multiparty election and unity government included opponents.
Parliamentary accountability follows the constitutional settlement he endorsed.
The revised constitution followed Constitutional Court scrutiny.
ANC alliance with unions did not transfer government selection to union leaders.
Political association and equal electoral rights preclude leadership exclusion by viewpoint.
His representative constitutional system allowed participation but did not establish voter repeal as an entitlement; mixed mechanisms warrant neutrality.
Collective cabinet and parliamentary authority contradict sole presidential policy power.
Constitutional parliamentary removal provides the relevant safeguard.
Fixed constitutional elections are inconsistent with unilateral postponement.
The settlement used representative accountability rather than an established general recall right; participation and stable mandates balance.
His single-term presidency exemplifies electoral and parliamentary accountability.
The civilian constitutional order rejects military replacement at soldiers' discretion.

axes.brief: The rights settlement strongly protected expression, assembly, privacy and judicial safeguards. Ordinary policing powers remained; not every risky personal choice was deregulated.
axes.counterEvidence: Actual police and immigration detention abuses documented in 1998 fell short of constitutional commitments; neither those abuses nor rights rhetoric alone determines every response.

answers.rationale: Bodily autonomy favours personal choice, while retained criminal regulation of drugs limits a categorical inference.
Proportionate court-supervised criminal investigation is compatible with rights limitations.
Peaceful unarmed demonstration has explicit constitutional protection.
Freedom of expression extends to criticism of government.
Bodily integrity weighs against compulsory measures primarily benefiting the individual.
Indiscriminate long-term tracking conflicts with constitutionally protected privacy.
Road safety protects other people and permits proportionate testing.
Liberty and prevention of serious harm pull in opposite directions; judicial safeguards alone do not settle pre-offence restraint.
Artistic and expressive freedom oppose censorship merely for moral offence.
Privacy supports anonymous communication by analogy, subject to investigation of actual offences.
Individual security and freedom from arbitrary searches weigh against suspicionless area searches.
Credible imminent disorder can justify narrowly limited assembly restrictions.
Privacy and judicially enforceable rights favour warrants outside emergencies.
Government accountability supports disclosure of misconduct, while legitimate confidentiality tempers the strength.

Mandela supported the 1994 voluntary gun hand-in campaign while licensed civilian ownership continued. His preference for reducing armed civilian violence and the retained permission create a mixed assessment of personal-defence ownership, even with screening.
Explicit protection against detention without trial rejects executive detention without review.

axes.brief: The presidency combined a shared South African identity with language, cultural and religious pluralism. Constitutional equality, rather than dominance by one community, set the limits.
axes.counterEvidence: Reconciliation and a common national identity were affirmative goals; Mandela did not endorse culturally separate communities overriding common rights.

answers.rationale: Plural constitutional citizenship rejects automatic cultural priority for the majority.
Language and cultural recognition imply reasonable public accommodation.
Participation in shared civic institutions did not require adopting one group's customs.
His reconciliation project included continuing Afrikaner and African identities.
Several official languages and equitable treatment oppose exclusive linguistic priority, while practicality remains relevant.
Recognition of indigenous languages supports acknowledging small indigenous communities.
Plural cultural recognition resists funding only predominant traditions.
Shared constitutional equality limits distinct practices when these conflict with national rights.
Equitable accommodation is preferable to an exclusively dominant calendar.
Several cultural traditions explicitly belonged in the new national identity.
Reconciliation through common institutions supports participation rather than isolation.
Language accommodation supports helpful local multilingual signage, limited by practical resources.
A common nation and continuing community identity were complementary, so neither takes categorical family priority.
Religious freedom supports accommodation where it does not defeat a proportionate safety purpose.
His nation-building embraced multiple cultural ways of life.
Integration should share civic rights without requiring cultural replacement.

axes.brief: Refugee protection and equal dignity favoured humanitarian admission, but the government retained immigration controls and deportations. Admission for ordinary workers cannot be inferred from anti-apartheid universalism alone.
axes.counterEvidence: Human Rights Watch documented detention, deportation and procedural failures. The 1998 refugee framework was a reform commitment, not evidence that all migrants already enjoyed effective protection.

answers.rationale: Capacity constraints support managed entry, but no universal strict annual cap follows from the humanitarian framework.
Equal dignity and regional cooperation support lawful movement to improve circumstances.
Refugees and family considerations make important skills an inadequate exclusive criterion.
Family dignity supports reunification within lawful migration rules.
Refugee protection rejects exclusion by skills or cultural origin, although protection is not automatically unconditional permanent residence.
Retained deportations contradict a blanket right to remain after unauthorised entry.
Employment needs and national capacity both mattered; neither unrestricted recruitment nor categorical reduction is inferred.
Housing obligations and migrant dignity create a conditional balance, not automatic reduction whenever services face pressure.
Humanitarian family unity weighs against a uniform cap displacing individual consideration.
Investor and employment openness support work entry, subject to retained controls.
Ordinary sponsorship may assist verification, while refugees and autonomous applicants require exceptions.
Education alone does not override retained immigration administration.
The refugee statute establishes protection distinct from ordinary economic admission.
Nonracial citizenship and protection reject cultural similarity as the governing preference.
Basic rights and social provision favour including lawful vulnerable migrants, although access remained contested.
Cultural pluralism supports equal treatment, but difference itself was not a numerical immigration objective.

axes.brief: Negotiated settlement and regional cooperation were priorities, but the Lesotho intervention shows conditional willingness to use force. The presidency retained and planned to modernise armed forces.
axes.counterEvidence: Peaceful reputation must not erase the intervention he approved and defended. Earlier armed struggle supplies context, not a direct measure of his presidency.

answers.rationale: Lesotho demonstrates force beyond self-defence, balanced by a strong preference for negotiated settlement.
His mediation approach supports diplomacy despite delays.
Modernisation supports capability, while reconstruction spending limits a pursuit of superiority at substantial cost.
Protection of people and constitutional order permits force against a well-evidenced imminent attack.
Approved regional intervention extended beyond responding to an attack on South Africa or an ally.
The new constitutional defence order favours accountable service over inherited mass male mobilisation.
Negotiated transitions show willingness to accept concessions to avoid violence.
Constitutional accountability and concern for human life suggest retaining meaningful human approval of lethal decisions. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Regional security duties qualify, but do not displace, a primarily protective defence purpose.
Lesotho and earlier armed resistance refute avoidance at every cost.
Regional peace operations require some sustained overseas capability.
His negotiated regional approach supports leaving claims unresolved rather than starting war.
Lesotho makes coercive leverage possible, while mediation prevents a general preference for threats.
His diplomatic practice ordinarily preferred preventing war over demonstrations of force.
Security intelligence has a legitimate role, but risking reconciliation for advantage merits a balanced inference.
Negotiated security cooperation supports reciprocal reductions that preserve protection.

axes.brief: Mandela supported international human rights, treaty cooperation and African regional institutions while preserving a sovereign constitutional state. Cooperation is stronger evidence than a commitment to supranational federation.
axes.counterEvidence: South Africa retained its currency and border administration; friendship and mediation across geopolitical blocs did not mean unconditional acceptance of every external decision.

answers.rationale: Constitutional supremacy and accepted international duties balance rather than establish unlimited domestic supremacy.
Binding cooperative rules fit his treaty-based reintegration, subject to consent and constitutional safeguards.
The constitution values international law but retains domestic constitutional adjudication; neither court automatically prevails in every conflict.
Regional security and global reintegration support enduring cooperative commitments.
Sovereign participation leaves a route to lawful withdrawal rather than permanent institutional permission.
Human-rights accountability favours binding international adjudication where jurisdiction is accepted.
Cooperation and universal rights weigh against routinely setting national advantage above common goals.
Cross-border environmental obligations fit cooperative international governance.
He supported regional coordination while retaining diplomatic independence, giving a conditional rather than categorical answer.
Rights-based reintegration supports international scrutiny capable of requiring domestic reform.
Maintaining national monetary institutions under GEAR supports currency autonomy.
SADC cooperation exemplifies shared resources and collective decisions.
National immigration control and accepted refugee obligations constrain each other.
Trade liberalisation and international reintegration favour negotiated common rules.
Regional cooperation did not imply dissolving national policy into a political federation.
His support for regional constitutional order favours collective enforcement beyond immediate advantage.

axes.brief: Governing policy was a mixed economy: social services and strategic public capacity alongside private enterprise, investment and selective privatisation. It was not the blanket nationalisation suggested by some earlier statements.
axes.counterEvidence: The RDP retained a major public role and basic-service obligations; privatisation was contested within the governing alliance.

answers.rationale: His governing shift towards investment and a mixed economy accepted a predominantly private commercial sector.
Universal basic-service delivery supports public ownership of essential networks where appropriate.
Cost and access rather than a universal ownership rule drove the mixed approach.
Public development enterprises were acceptable, but not an automatic replacement for private competition.
Expanding basic public healthcare implies retaining substantial publicly owned facilities.
Strategic infrastructure remains a plausible public responsibility in the mixed model.
Efficiency and selective private participation support equivalent lower-cost contracting.
Public development finance can coexist with commercial banks in a mixed economy.
Selective sales formed part of governing economic restructuring.

His programme supported housing delivery and a mixed economy, but publicly supported home ownership is not the same as a substantial publicly owned rental sector. Public provision and private ownership therefore yield a conditional answer for this specific tenure model.
The investment-friendly approach permits private strategic suppliers under effective regulation.
Land and resource reform favour public stewardship, while governing rejection of wholesale nationalisation balances general ownership.
Efficiency-based contracting is consistent with the public-private mix.
Essential strategic capacity can justify retention despite sale proceeds.
Fiscal discipline and restructuring support sale where continued subsidy produces no public justification.
A plural constitutional public sphere and inherited public broadcasting favour a public broadcaster alongside private media.

axes.brief: GEAR moved towards lower trade barriers and foreign investment. Development objectives and the negotiated transition leave room for limited exceptions.
axes.counterEvidence: Earlier ANC economic nationalism and labour concerns persisted, but the scored period is the presidency that adopted liberalisation.

answers.rationale: The governing liberalisation programme weighs against ordinary protective tariffs.
GEAR explicitly promoted trade opening despite adjustment costs.
Domestic development and procurement value compete; neither universal preference follows.
International reintegration supports sourcing on favourable commercial terms.
Supply security can justify exceptions but does not imply routine exclusion of cheaper imports.
Accelerated liberalisation supports some unilateral opening within a wider integration strategy.
Development support can be justified temporarily, balanced by the shift away from trade insulation.
Courting overseas investment supports broadly comparable market access.
Rural development mattered, but blanket agricultural import restrictions do not follow from land reform.
Investment and competitiveness policy expects firms to adjust to external competition.
Negotiated rules and reciprocal enforcement balance rather than establish automatic retaliation.
Equal product taxation fits a more open trading framework.
Rules against unfair subsidies can coexist with the chosen trade opening.
Lower tariffs were central to international economic reintegration.
Strategic control and investment attraction have competing weight in the mixed economy.
Trade openness supports foreign digital services by analogy, subject to ordinary domestic regulation.

axes.brief: GEAR favoured market allocation and monetary stability while retaining development programmes and labour protections. The RDP was not a command-production system.
axes.counterEvidence: Mandela defended state-led reconstruction and labour representation; fiscal discipline did not erase social obligations.

answers.rationale: The investment-led economy leaves ordinary production to firms.
Compulsory industrial output targets conflict with the governing market orientation.
Macroeconomic stabilisation assumed substantial market price formation.
Development and infrastructure programmes support steering selected investment.
Demand and commercial sustainability were important to restructuring.
Essential access can justify intervention, while market supply also mattered; conditional price controls merit neutrality.
Encouraging investment supports entry without a general production-need test.
Development lending is plausible, but coercively directing all commercial banks does not follow.
Relaxation of exchange controls supports greater freedom to move capital, without implying full deregulation.
Reconstruction can support targeted development subsidies.
Stable national currency and monetary institutions weigh against private currencies replacing public control.
Labour protections and wage-floor concerns support a legal minimum, even though no comprehensive national minimum was enacted then.
Collective bargaining rights explicitly support negotiated wages.
GEAR monetary stability and constitutional reserve-bank independence weigh against routine plan-directed interest rates.
Affordable housing obligations balance market pricing; no blanket national rent rule is inferred.
Ordinary industrial production remained substantially market-led rather than centrally distributed.

axes.brief: Mandela sought material redress, social grants and land reform, constrained by fiscal stabilisation. Redistribution is assessed separately from public ownership and social-service spending.
axes.counterEvidence: GEAR spending restraint and investor confidence limited immediate transfers; the assessment should not turn anti-apartheid egalitarianism into maximal cash redistribution.

answers.rationale: Redressing inherited poverty supports meaningful tax-and-transfer redistribution.
Equalising opportunity and conditions gives some justification for progressive taxation.
Social-assistance rights support a stronger floor within sustainable resources.
A basic floor and broader social participation both mattered, so neither extreme defines benefits.
Progressive fiscal capacity fits his redress objectives.
Economic incentives and social redress both mattered under GEAR.
Funding assistance through large estates fits redress while respecting property rights.
Work and self-reliance matter, but continuing inability to meet needs resists an automatic cut-off.
Wealth inequality suggests progressive funding, balanced by investment and property protections.
Fiscal restraint and social obligations pulled in opposite directions.
Dignity and inclusion support assistance beyond mere survival.
Fiscal competitiveness and expanding assistance were both objectives.
Supporting low-paid households fits poverty reduction alongside employment.
Progressive contributions are more consistent with redress than uniform marginal rates.
Compensated land reform is explicitly accommodated by the constitution.
Targeting scarce funds and addressing wider low-income exclusion warrant a conditional balance.

axes.brief: The constitutional settlement protected equal belief and civil authority, with voluntary religious observance and compatible recognition of religious family practices. Secular law did not require religion to vanish from public life.
axes.counterEvidence: Mandela respected faith communities; constitutional permission for voluntary worship qualifies strictly exclusionary secularism.

answers.rationale: Equal belief and constitutional rights provide a public justification independent of one faith.
No particular doctrine acquired general lawmaking authority.
Religious leaders had no constitutional veto over government.
Equal religious freedom rejects a single foundational state religion.
Equitable instruction about beliefs fits the settlement.

An officially recognised state faith cultivated by public schools conflicts with the settlement’s equal freedom of conscience and plural religious treatment. This does not assume that the instruction must be compulsory.
Civil constitutional courts retain authority over legal disputes.
Consultation is compatible with pluralism; official clerical legislative review is not required.
Voluntary equitable observance was expressly permitted in state institutions.
Equal accommodation may receive support, but promoting faith as such is not an established general duty.
State endorsement of one religion sits uneasily with equitable treatment.
Inherited holidays and plural equality balance; retention need not be official endorsement.
Government office derives from constitutional appointment or election rather than clerical status.
Religious freedom and equal fiscal treatment leave conditional room for exemptions, not automatic privilege.
Bodily freedom and civil equality oppose mandatory religious permission to marry.
Compatible religious family-law arrangements could receive civil recognition under constitutional rights.

axes.brief: Nonracialism, gender equality, reproductive choice and protection against sexual-orientation discrimination support substantial social reform. Mandela also valued family, elders and cultural continuity.
axes.counterEvidence: Constitutional equality is not proof that he personally endorsed every later marriage, adoption or gender-language policy; these are moderate principle-based inferences.

answers.rationale: Transforming discriminatory customs was central to the new rights order.
Rights reform takes precedence where inherited practices conflict with equality.
Protection across marital status supports equal recognition of varied households.

Gender equality and women’s participation weigh against encouraging fixed sex-specific roles as a social norm. His respect for family and voluntary cultural practice qualifies the inference; the question concerns encouragement, not legal enforcement.
Sexual-orientation equality supports extending civil marriage by inference; it was not enacted during his presidency.
Respect for family coexisted with equality across household forms.
The early-abortion law expressly protected the woman's choice.
Children's equality and education constrain parental vetoes based solely on traditional sexual values.
Sexual-orientation equality supports adoption assessed by parenting capacity.
Cultural respect and personal liberty balance rather than dictate one public dress standard.
Equal dignity supports accommodating self-identification without assuming his endorsement of every later convention.
Shared ethical inheritance and reform of discriminatory norms were both valued.
Gender equality supports equal acceptance across conventional roles.
Negotiated implementation mattered, but urgent rights reforms prevent a categorical gradualism.
Inclusive education follows non-discrimination, though modern curricula are inferred rather than recorded.
His reconciliation and cultural recognition preserve intergenerational connections where compatible with rights.

axes.brief: Reconstruction favoured infrastructure and productive science, while constitutional environmental rights, bodily integrity and informed consent justify precaution for irreversible medical risks. These are historical analogies, not recorded technology-policy answers.
axes.counterEvidence: Growth and urgent housing needs prevent maximal precaution; consent alone does not establish that basic safety is sufficient for healthy-person enhancement.

answers.rationale: Economic development favours useful technology while protected health and environmental rights require conditions on uncertain scale-up. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Reasonable evidence gathering follows duties to protect future generations, without requiring certainty. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Justifiable social development can warrant some habitat loss under the constitutional balance. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Bodily integrity supports studying serious long-term medical risks before widespread use. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Productivity-led development supports adoption with retraining and social protection. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
The constitution balances conservation with justified social and economic development. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Potential food and environmental benefits balance unproven consequences, so a conditional pilot-to-adoption approach is inferred. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Enhancement offers less urgent benefit than therapy, making long-term safety evidence a defensible precaution. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Growth supports technical solutions while environmental duties do not justify dismissing consumption measures. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Environmental rights support delaying poorly understood impacts for assessment. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Informed consent and bodily protection suggest basic tests alone are insufficient for invasive elective enhancement. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Equal healthcare protection supports testing performance across patient groups before clinical scale-up. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.

Scientific freedom supports controlled research, while intergenerational bodily risks and consent constraints counterbalance enhancement. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Protecting future ecological conditions supports substantial ecosystem evidence. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Urgent housing and transport programmes support development subject to reasonable environmental conditions. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Irreversible harm attracts stronger precautions under duties to health and future generations. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.

axes.brief: The 1996 settlement combined national transformation with constitutionally protected provincial and municipal government. Powers were shared under the constitution rather than left to presidential discretion.
axes.counterEvidence: ANC preferences for national unity and nationwide social rights limited local autonomy; negotiated provincial rights were nevertheless real.

answers.rationale: Protected provincial powers matter even where the national government disagrees.
Constitutional allocation and courts, rather than an automatic national executive trump, settle jurisdiction.
National unity weighs against a general unilateral regional exit right.
Nationwide constitutional obligations justify defined intervention rather than unrestricted local obstruction.
Provincial constitutions were expressly allowed within the national order.
The constitutional national police service supports national coordination with provincial responsibilities.
Redistributive fiscal sharing limits keeping most locally generated revenue.
National education standards support equality alongside provincial administration.
Provincial and local fiscal powers permit some differing rates.
Common labour rights support nationwide employment standards.
Municipal constitutional status does not give voters an unrestricted power to change jurisdictions without legal approval.
Equal basic healthcare supports national coverage standards.
Recognition of traditional institutions supports compatible local customary governance.
National fiscal coordination justifies limits on harmful regional tax competition.
Shared environmental powers allow regional management where wider effects are absent.
A multiregional disaster requires national coordination consistent with constitutional cooperative government.

axes.brief: Mandela explained social exclusion and violence through apartheid institutions, deprivation and learned relations, supporting socially shaped behaviour. The inferences concern causal beliefs, not environmental protection or a claim that biology has no role.
axes.counterEvidence: His emphasis on dignity and individual character does not quantify every psychological trait; temperament is balanced because personal dispositions and transformative surroundings both fit his account.

answers.rationale: His account of deprivation and social conflict gives upbringing and surroundings greater explanatory weight.

His account of unequal schooling and institutional opportunity favours social explanations of national differences. This is a limited extension of that account, not a direct statement about the genetic contribution to IQ.
Dismantling gender discrimination implies a substantial role for imposed expectations.
Experience of repression and insecurity supports a social explanation of stress differences, without denying biology.
Education and opportunity were intended to open interests previously constrained by apartheid.
Risk-taking in struggle is intelligible through circumstances and experience rather than chiefly heredity.
Reconciliation deliberately built cooperation across previously segregated groups.
His effort to cultivate mutual understanding suggests empathy can be socially developed.
Education and material conditions provide a modest inference towards socially shaped attention.
The transformation of racial attitudes supports moral judgements shaped by social learning.
Reconciliation sought to change learned perceptions of other communities as threats.
Individual temperament and social transformation both mattered; his record supports no categorical primacy for this particular trait.
Cross-cultural recognition suggests learned standards have substantial influence on attractiveness.
His explanation of political violence centred oppressive conditions, rejecting inherited racial criminality.
Education and reconstruction were intended to develop self-control and civic habits beyond racial classifications.
Gender equality and anti-discrimination policy locate unequal rewards substantially in imposed opportunities and expectations.

review.notes: Independently read all 240 item rationales against exact wording and all 15 briefs/counterarguments. Checked the Foundation’s economic and Lesotho accounts and SA History Online’s presidential record. Kept the 1994–1999 scope, distinguishing earlier nationalisation rhetoric and armed struggle from mixed-economy government and conditional regional intervention. Corrected publicly supported housing versus public rental ownership, encouragement versus enforcement of sex roles, and an overstrong national-IQ inference. Removed an unwarranted compulsory qualifier from religious schooling. Neutral economic, immigration and medical answers reflect competing documented rights, fiscal and administrative principles. Modern equality and technology positions are explicitly principle-based inferences, not later enactments attributed to Mandela. Portrait and full-catalogue similarity are checked during integration. Rechecked his support for the 1994 gun hand-in campaign and retained a mixed firearm answer grounded in that campaign versus continued licensed ownership. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.
